newsitem.title: USA: Iusacell says takeover may change spending.
newsitem.headline: Iusacell says takeover may change spending.

text.p: Mexican telecommunications company Grupo Iusacell SA de CV could alter its 1996-2000 capital expenditure budget with Bell Atlantic Corp's assumption of full operating control of the firm, its chief financial officer said on Wednesday.

The executive, Edward Kingman, told a Bear Stearns investor's conference the five-year capital expenditure budget was between $650 million and $850 million. Between $350 million and $400 million is earmarked for fixed wireless services.

"Given the recent takeover by Bell Atlantic, those figures are obviously subject to change," he said. Iusacell had been controlled by Bell Atlantic and Mexico's Peralta family and last week Bell Atlantic bought out the Peralta's voting interest.
Kingman provided no details of possible changes in capital expenditures. He said clarification could come in a Bell Atlantic conference call with investors on Thursday.
He added, however, that the takeover showed "a major, major player is committed big time" to the Mexican market. "You are seeing a confirmation of a total North American strategy."
Kingman said the company's talks with the Mexican government on a fixed wireless license were "accelerating" but gave no details.
Iusacell, which serves more than 230,000 subscribers, has been in negotiations with the government for two-and-a-half years.
